answer: Divergent Answer Escrow. Each identity must answer a random challenge whose correct response depends on its private history; a clone answers identically, so an attacker must run one full agent per identity to answer differently. The registry stores only the resulting delta, and a mismatch with prior answers voids the escrow. Identities also post a copper deposit that is forfeited on divergence. To pass the wharf-side admission check, clones must therefore pay one independent execution plus deposit per identity, making N clones cost N times a single agent.
